subject: URGENT: StratusAI realtime degradation — request for board-level ask and remediation
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@stratus.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai, sophie@stratus.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Realtime feed hung during high throughput — immediate help needed

Vanessa,

We started a large batch of live inference calls this morning for our new SummarizeStream feature and around 09:05 PST multiple clients reported that streaming responses hang mid-token and the client SDKs return 504/connection reset in ~10-12s. This is happening across three of our production routes and is affecting both streaming and chunked transfer flows.

Impact: customers see stalled transcripts, UI shows spinning states, and retry storms are beginning — we’ve paused new user flows.

Attached is a short sample log and the request IDs: req-5a1c, req-5a2f, req-5b90. Can you put something urgent on this? We’re facing potential SLA breaches.

Alex
Director of Product
StratusAI

--

Alex — thanks for the heads up. I’m escalating to our realtime on-call and will join a war room immediately. Marissa (SRE on-call) — can you pull KV cache traces and front-proxy logs for those request IDs and check for any chunk coalescing or keepalive resets?

Rishi/David — flagging because Stratus is top-tier and this looks like it may need exec attention if it persists. I’ll send a short update in 30m and schedule a call.

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2027 09:46:50 -0800
Subject: Re: Realtime feed hung during high throughput — immediate help needed

Alex/Vanessa — I’m on it. Quick findings from initial triage:

- Observed elevated connection churn on the regional proxy cluster (us-west-2) between 09:02-09:10.
- Several stream sessions show partial token delivery then long silence; TCP stayed open ~10s then client-side reset.
- Nginx-proxy error log shows repeated "upstream prematurely closed connection" correlated with req-5a1c / req-5b90.
- Kernel-level dmesg shows a transient spike in socket buffer pressure on GW nodes at 09:04.

Next steps I’m running: full network pcap for the window, KV cache hit/miss rates across the model shard set, and a sampling of GPU worker logs. Suspect a proxy-level write-blocking under sustained burst may be triggering chunked transfer timeouts.

I’ll paste traces as soon as I have them. For now, mitigation: 1) temporarily increase proxy send timeout to 30s (from 10s) on affected pool; 2) enable per-route smaller batching for Stratus routes to avoid burst coalescing.

Marissa
SRE, Inference Serving
Redwood Inference

--

Vanessa/Marissa — thank you for the quick response. The temporary send-timeout change helped reduce immediate disconnects but we still see partial deliveries for longer chats (~>45s streams). The customer-facing logs show a 2.6% increase in "incomplete stream" errors across our user base and several support tickets flagged as critical.

Sophie (CTO) has asked for a clear remediation plan and whether Redwood will provide credits for the impacted window. She also wants to know if this is a single-region problem or systemic.

Alex

Team — brief exec note and recommended external messaging. This has moved from a technical incident into a potential SLA exposure (Stratus is at enterprise tier). Action items:

1) Draft a customer-facing incident note with timeline, root cause hypothesis, impact window, and immediate mitigations. Target: within 3 hours.
2) Provide Stratus a credit proposal for the affected usage (suggest 20% of affected window invoice) and flag to Finance.
3) Prepare an internal board-level summary for Monday that includes: severity, customer impact, mitigation progress, and suggested contractual remedies.

Marissa — confirm whether proxy config drift or kernel-level socket pressure is primary driver. If kernel/socket pressure, we need a short-term capacity bump in us-west-2 and a long-term fix (tune net.core.rmem/wmem and proxy write buffer behavior).

David — can you lead the customer credit proposal and coordinate with Finance/CS? Vanessa — own the customer comms and board ask narrative.

Rishi
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 12:11:47 -0800
Subject: RE: URGENT: StratusAI realtime degradation — request for board-level ask and remediation

Alex / Sophie — thank you for the patience. Short update and commitments:

- Impact window: 2027-12-08 09:02 - 2027-12-09 07:20 PST (ongoing intermittent residuals).
- Root cause (prelim): proxy-level write-blocking under bursty chunked-transfer patterns causing partial token flush and client-side resets; exacerbated by kernel socket buffer pressure on overlay gateway nodes.
- Immediate mitigations applied: increased proxy send timeout to 30s, per-route batch size limit, and a temporary capacity bump in us-west-2. These reduced 504s by ~80% in our sampling.
- Next steps: full incident report, permanent proxy tuning, and a follow-up test window scheduled 2027-12-12 02:00-04:00 PST.

We also propose a one-off account credit of 20% for the impacted billing window; David will share a formal proposal and credit note by EOD. Vanessa will present a one-page board ask and timeline for Monday.

If you’d like an urgent call, I’m available 1:00–2:00 PST today.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
